decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach toward one support on each side; orient grippers forward/down before visual alignment.
Align above the rear left and outer right white supports. Descend only to a preliminary grasp height; confirm in wrist views.
Match the supports' yaw while compensating the link6-to-finger offset. Fine alignment remains uncertain until the next wrist view.
Center each block between the fingers, close fully, then make a small test lift to verify retention visually.
Both blocks follow the test lift. Carry them inward above the intended base positions and square their yaw, keeping the grippers closed.
Lower both upright supports to table height at symmetric base locations, then release without lateral motion.
Withdraw upward from the released supports, then separate and rotate toward opposing end grasps on the long board.
The base supports remain upright. Complete inward-facing board-grasp orientations and approach the long board ends from above.
Descend symmetrically onto the long board ends, close both grippers fully, and test a small level lift.
Lift the retained long board above the supports, then translate it level toward their shared centerline.
Set the long board gently across the two supports, open both grippers, and withdraw a short distance to check stability.
Lower board appears stable. Clear it upward and reorient each arm toward the remaining white block in its own workspace.
Replan from the interrupted pose with smaller rotations. Move above the two remaining supports, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Align each gripper with its remaining block's long axis and approach a preliminary grasp height, avoiding the completed lower board.
Correct lateral alignment from wrist views, first clearing the right gripper from the board edge, then descend slowly around both blocks.
Right arm is contacting the board; withdraw outward and upward before a new approach. Fine-align and test-lift the left block independently.
The left block is retained. Lift clear and carry it over the lower board's left middle-support position; hold the right arm clear while reassessing the displaced block.
Place and release the left middle support. Reorient the right gripper above the displaced block, approaching from the outside instead of over the board.
Withdraw the left arm from its released support. Descend on the right block from its outside end, keeping clear of the lower board.
Right wrist shows the block off-center toward one jaw. Lift slightly, shift along the jaw axis, and approach again without pushing the board.
Fine-center the right block between the jaws, close fully, and test a short vertical lift; retention will be checked visually.
The right block is centered and follows the gripper. Lift it well above the board before rotating and carrying it toward the right middle-support location.
Carry the right support above its placement point while squaring its orientation. Move the empty left arm toward the middle-board approach.
Lower and release the right middle support onto the board. Finish aligning the empty left gripper above the next board's end.
Clear the released right support upward before turning toward the middle board. Lower the open left gripper to its end-grasp height.
Both middle supports appear upright. Complete the right end-grasp orientation above the loose middle board while the left waits open.
Bring the right gripper to the board end, close both grippers fully, and test a small synchronized lift.
Lift the middle board level above the upright supports, then carry it toward the tower with both grippers closed.
Center the middle board above both supports and lower it level to their tops, retaining the grasp until placement is checked.
Release the centered middle board and separate upward. Approach the green and small wooden top pieces from their respective outside workspaces.
Move above each top piece. Orient the right gripper along the small board's long direction for a narrow-width grasp, while aligning the left with the green piece.
Use wrist views to square both top pieces with the jaws and compensate the fingertip offset while descending cautiously.
Adjust grasp depth and lateral centering for both top pieces, close fully, and perform a short test lift to check retention.
Both top pieces follow the grippers. Lift clear, then carry the small board inward while rotating it level across the tower; keep the green piece safely to the left.
Center the small board above the middle layer and finish its level yaw rotation. Stage the green piece above the left side, clear of the placement path.
Lower the small board onto the center of the completed middle layer. Keep the green piece staged clear and verify seating before release.
Release the seated small board and withdraw the right arm outward. Carry the green cap above its center, keeping it level and closed in the left gripper.
Fine-center and lower the green cap onto the small board. Start returning the empty right arm toward its origin without crossing the tower.
Open the left gripper to release the seated green cap and withdraw clear. Return the right arm to origin while keeping both grippers open.
The released tower remains upright in RGB. Return the left arm along a gradual elbow-up path and settle the right arm at origin, with both grippers open.
Complete the left arm's gradual return to origin, keeping both grippers open and leaving the tower undisturbed.
